boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Albemarle Sound record (May 5, 1864) in Operations Against Plymouth [April-May 1864]: the action between the ram Albemarle, with the Bombshell and Cotton Plant, and Melancton Smith's gunboats off the mouth of the Roanoke. The April 17-20 capture of Plymouth is the separate record NC012 and is not added here. The live NPS campaign header and its April-May dates do not replace the frozen campaign or interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to one record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 9 gunboats against a Confederate ram; the live Forces Engaged field reads zero. NPS says the Albemarle fought seven blockading Union ships. Smith's May 2 order of attack lists eight vessels (Miami, Ceres, Commodore Hull, Seymour, Mattabesett, Sassacus, Wyalusing, Whitehead), and his report says the Mattabesett, Wyalusing, Whitehead and Sassacus got underway to engage the ram, the steamer Cotton Plant with troops and the armed steamer Bombshell. Cooke says he saw six gunboats and then three more double-enders carrying ten to twelve guns each, and that he had the Bombshell as tender and the Cotton Plant under convoy.
claims.rationale: Vessel counts from a table, a summary and two interested reports; no crew or armament return was inspected. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; the live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Smith says the ram came out of the Roanoke at 2 p.m. and was drawn ten miles down the sound by his picket force before the action; Cooke says he saw the gunboats about ten miles off as he reached the river's mouth. Smith says side-wheel steamers could not be laid alongside the Albemarle without disabling their wheels, and that darkness ended the action at about 7:30.
claims.rationale: Water, distance and light described by the two commanders; no chart or log was inspected.

claims.value: Before the action Smith reported the ram in the Roanoke with three steamers and 30 barges 'said to be ready' to cooperate, and afterward had no positive information about rebel barges reported at the mouth of the Croatan (the compiler queries Chowan). He says the smaller vessels answered signals without obeying them, and that a signal from the Wyalusing that she was sinking, which he learned only later was wrong, deterred further ramming. Cooke says the smoke kept him from seeing the damage he did, and he learned by flag of truce that no one on the Bombshell was hurt.
claims.rationale: Contemporary reports of what each commander knew or believed; the signal logs were not inspected.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Melancton Smith (Captain) and J. W. Cooke (Commander); the live page gives 'Captain James Cooke', and the frozen ranks are kept. Smith signs as senior officer in the sounds and says he tried ramming, as the Department suggested, with the Sassacus, and was deterred from repeating it; the Miami was ordered to explode her torpedo but did not. Cooke reports to Commander Pinkney and credits pilot Hopkins with bringing the vessel back.
claims.rationale: Roles attributed by the inspected reports. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit; Roe of the Sassacus and the Miami's commander are named as attributed actors only through Smith's report (Roe's own report was not selected).

claims.value: The frozen result is Inconclusive; the live Results field reads 'Indecisive', and NPS calls the action a draw, with the Bombshell recaptured and the Sassacus badly damaged. Smith says his efforts to capture the ram failed, that his shot had no perceptible effect, and that he drove her into the Roanoke; he reports the Bombshell captured with 37 prisoners on May 6 and with 33 on May 24. Cooke says the Bombshell was forced to surrender, the muzzle of his after gun was broken, and he believes he sank one of the enemy's most formidable boats and crippled two others. Smith times the action from 4:40 to about 7:30; Cooke from twenty minutes to five until after dark.
claims.rationale: Opposed interested accounts; Cooke's sinking claim is his belief. The two Smith prisoner counts differ and are kept. Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty field reads 88 total; the live page reads zero. Smith's May 6 letter gives his loss in 'the large vessel' as 5 killed and 26 wounded, before returns from the Sassacus; the Mattabesett surgeon's list names two killed and six wounded (a count of the names). The Bombshell's crew was captured (37 or 33 prisoners, above). Cooke reports only that no one on the Bombshell was hurt; no Albemarle casualty figure is in the selected reports.
claims.rationale: The frozen 88's basis is not established and is not reconciled with the partial Union figures or the prisoners. The live zero is not measured absence. Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Roe's Sassacus report and the other ship commanders' reports, the logs, Davenport's May 7 report and Lee's May 14 transmittal (read, not selected), Smith's May 9-June 4 letters, and any Confederate casualty return for the Albemarle remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Wessells's dispatch and report (Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIII), Cooke's reports and Melancton Smith's reports (Official Records of the Navies, Series I, Volume 9) are separate families of interested participants' accounts; the volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. No 19th-century history was inspected for this campaign. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
